newsitem.title: INDIA: British model pardoned in India looks to new life.
newsitem.headline: British model pardoned in India looks to new life.

text.p: British model Samantha Slater, released after two years in an Indian jail on drugs charges, said on Monday she now wanted to take up social work and anti-drugs campaigning and was leaving her boyfriend.
Slater, 25, a British fashion model until two years ago when she was arrested in India carrying drugs, said prison life had changed her outlook and life for the better.

"I don't think I have lost anything (in life). I want to do social work, especially anti-drug campaigns for the youth," the dark haired ex-model from Birmingham told reporters at a news conference on Monday.
Slater was released on Thursday, following a mercy petition and signature campaign by her mother in Britain.
Indian police arrested her in January 1994 for carrying two ounces of cannabis resin hidden in her brassiere while on a motorbike tour of Kerala, southern India, with her boyfriend Andrew Kershaw.
Slater pleaded not guilty to the charges, but was sentenced to 10 years' imprisonment under India's Narcotics Control Act. Kershaw was sentenced to three.
"Prison life made me a calmer person," said Slater who was dressed in a black Indian flowing dress with a chiffon jacket and was wearing light lipstick.
She said her attitude to life had changed and Kershaw was no longer her boyfriend. "I have drifted away from my boyfriend. He is a closed chapter," she said.
She said while she managed to remain strong and positive, Kershaw had become frustrated, one of the reasons why she was leaving him.
Life in Indian jail had also transformed her culturally and spiritually, she said.
She said she had mastered the art of wearing the Indian sari and it would be difficult for her to return to revealing western clothes which she once wore as a glamarous model.

"I began to read a variety of subjects, including religion and spiritualism," said Slater, frequently smiling during the news conference attended by dozens of journalists, organised by the British high commission office in Madras.
She said her first year in prison was "nightmarish" and she lost a lot of weight. But she made a lot of friends among inmates.
She learnt Malayalam, the local language of Kerala, while in return she taught English to the jail inmates.
She kept in touch with home by reading British newspapers which came to her by mail from home. She said she took special interest in the divorce of Prince Charles and Lady Diana.
"I turned vegetarian in jail and intend to remain one," she said. Banana skin curry and rice was her regular meal.
Her arrest had evoked strong passion back home with her mother organising fashion shows to collect more than 10,000 pounds ($15,640) to work on her release.
The Bishop of Birmingham, Rev Peter Hawkins started a campaign for her release by contacting a Syrian Christian priest in Thrissur town, where she was jailed.
Slater returns to Britain on Wednesday but says she would like to come back to India on another visit. "But this time I might have problems getting a visa," she said. ($1=.6393 Pound)
